title: RAG paper
text: RAG combines a parametric language model with retrieved non-parametric information. Retrieval supplies context for generation; a fluent response alone does not establish that the retrieved evidence supports it.

title: Attention Is All You Need
text: Transformer encoder outputs feed decoder cross-attention as keys and values; decoder representations supply queries. Masked decoder self-attention prevents access to subsequent positions. Training can process shifted target tokens in parallel, whereas autoregressive inference generates new tokens sequentially. Learned embedding tables convert token IDs to vectors.

title: Semantic search
text: Semantic search embeds documents and queries into a compatible vector space and retrieves nearby document vectors. The query/document encoders and similarity measure must be compatible. Similarity is not proof that a passage answers the question.

title: Faiss indexes
text: Faiss provides exact and approximate vector indexes. Inverted-file indexes group vectors; product quantization compresses vectors into codes. Clustering and quantization can share techniques but serve different retrieval and compression objectives. Index choices trade accuracy, memory and speed.

title: Tokenization algorithms
text: Tokenizers split text into tokens and map tokens to vocabulary IDs. IDs are identifiers, not semantic coordinates. Tokenization depends on the tokenizer and text boundaries. Model layers transform token embeddings into context-sensitive representations.

title: BERT model configuration
text: BERT exposes hidden_size as a model configuration dimension. Token IDs are mapped through model embeddings; hidden states are vectors. A vector store stores/indexes these outputs; it does not choose what semantic features an already-trained encoder learns.

title: Redis persistence
text: Redis offers RDB snapshots and AOF logging, with different durability and recovery tradeoffs. An in-memory cache is not automatically a durable system of record. Select durability, eviction and recovery behavior explicitly instead of assuming all cached data survives.

title: Caching strategies
text: Write-through updates a cache when the underlying data changes; lazy loading populates it on demand. Cache updates add write work and can cache unused data. Cache TTL expires entries; it is not by itself a reliable write-back-to-database mechanism.

title: Dynamo paper
text: Dynamo partitions keys using consistent hashing and virtual nodes. A physical server owns multiple ring positions. Membership changes transfer affected key ranges; they do not generally rehash every key. Virtual nodes improve distribution but can involve multiple physical neighbors.

title: DNS concepts — RFC 1034
text: DNS resolution uses resolvers, authoritative name servers and referrals through the namespace hierarchy, with caching. Root and top-level-domain servers provide delegation information; a recursive resolver follows the relevant referrals. It is not an arbitrary all-provider broadcast.

title: API Gateway WebSocket quotas
text: WebSocket gateway capacity depends on connection arrival rate, connection duration and service limits. The documented managed-service limits are specific to AWS API Gateway, not universal limits for every TCP server. Horizontal scaling and per-connection resource budgets need workload measurements.

title: SQS message queues
text: A message queue decouples producers and consumers and holds pending work durably. Queues help asynchronous processing; not every synchronous service request needs a queue. Consumers must account for delivery semantics, retries and idempotency.

title: Apache Flink overview
text: Flink performs stateful processing on bounded or unbounded streams. A stream processor computes on events; a queue or broker transports/buffers events. They can be complementary rather than interchangeable components.

title: JSON Web Signature — RFC 7515
text: JWS supports digital signatures and MACs. With asymmetric signatures, the signing party uses its private key and a verifier uses the corresponding public key. Who owns the signing key depends on the actual issuer; not all JWTs use asymmetric signatures.

title: HTTP Live Streaming — RFC 8216
text: HLS uses playlists that identify media segments. EXTINF describes a segment duration and EXT-X-MEDIA-SEQUENCE identifies the first segment sequence number. Clients fetch the referenced segments; playlists may update during live streaming.

title: DynamoDB read consistency
text: NoSQL is not a single consistency model. DynamoDB tables and local secondary indexes offer eventual or strong read consistency, while global secondary indexes and streams have different constraints. Explain the chosen database and operation rather than calling every NoSQL database weakly consistent.

title: Amazon S3 object storage
text: S3 stores objects in buckets and exposes object retrieval APIs. An image-search feature also needs searchable representations and an index; choosing object storage for image bytes does not itself implement semantic image similarity search.

title: Redis key eviction
text: Fast key lookup does not remove RAM capacity limits. Redis maxmemory and eviction policies bound cache growth; replication and persistence buffers can require additional memory. Estimate object counts, payloads and overhead independently of lookup complexity.
